title: Work IQ: Context IQ adds agents, skills and content sources to the prompt menu
summary: Hold: the agent inventory API is presented without its documented Microsoft Agent 365 licence requirement. The briefing also treats agent usage costs as unconfirmed even though Microsoft publishes licensing and metering rules for agents in Copilot Chat; uncertainty should be limited to the new menu interaction.

claims.where: What's changing; front matter: changes; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this particular expansion or identify its additional menu entries.
claims.quote: Searched: ExpandedContextIQ; Context IQ 570854; Context IQ agents skills content sources. Read release-notes search excerpts, the Context IQ support article, Work IQ overview and Build skills for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat; none identifies this roadmap expansion.

claims.claim: The 10 March 2026 Copilot release notes document selecting a Teams channel in Context IQ to ground a Copilot Chat prompt.
claims.quote: Context IQ now allows you to search for and select Microsoft Teams channels when creating prompts in Copilot Chat, so responses are grounded in a specific channel instead of across all Teams content.

claims.claim: Typing / in the Copilot Chat compose box opens the references interaction.
claims.quote: To reference a specific piece of information, type **/** and begin typing the people, file, meeting, or email you wish to link.

claims.claim: The existing references menu offers files, people, meetings and emails.
claims.quote: People, Microsoft 365 files, meetings, and emails are accessible through tabs.

claims.claim: The existing menu includes Teams chats and channels.
claims.quote: Copilot suggests your relevant Teams group and meeting chats based on recent activity and number of participants under the **Chats** tab. Copilot also displays your recently used Teams channels under the **Channels** tab.

claims.claim: The existing menu includes SharePoint sites and lists.
claims.quote: Copilot displays SharePoint sites, pages, and lists that you've recently interacted with or were shared with you. Select a site to scope your prompt to its contents.

claims.claim: Copilot connector content can be selected from the existing references menu.
claims.quote: You can now ground your Copilot prompts on third-party data using your organization's Graph Connector content, accessible from the references menu in Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The cited support article does not list agents or skills as reference types.
claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ agents skills content sources; read the complete Refer to specific files and more in Microsoft Copilot article. Its content-type sections cover people, meetings, Teams, emails, files/images, SharePoint and connectors, not agents or skills.

claims.claim: The references menu suggests content by scanning files, emails, conversations and other Microsoft 365 apps and services.
claims.quote: When you initiate the references menu, relevant content is suggested based on scanning of your files, emails, conversations, and other Microsoft 365 apps and services.

claims.claim: Copilot refers to content the user includes as part of its response.
claims.quote: Copilot refers to the content you include as part of its response.

claims.claim: Licensed users can use the per-user Work IQ button at the top right of chat to enable references to people, files, meetings and emails.
claims.quote: At the top right of the chat page, make sure the **Work IQ** button is turned on.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Only files are available to reference when Work IQ is turned off.
claims.quote: Only files are available to reference when you've turned off **Work IQ** in chat.

claims.claim: Users without a Microsoft Copilot licence can reference only files in the existing references menu.
claims.quote: Only files are available to reference for users without a Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview describes user-scoped actions limited to what that user may see or do.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview says every tool invocation is logged and evaluated.
claims.quote: Every tool invocation is logged and evaluated, enabling auditability, usage analytics, rate limiting, and real-time compliance enforcement across agents and data sources.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft has not connected the expanded Context IQ selection mechanism to the Work IQ API identity and invocation-logging mechanisms.
claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ agents skills rollout identity actions block menu. Read Work IQ overview, Context IQ support, agent management and Chat skills documentation; none specifies the identity or API invocation path for this expansion.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified the read or action capabilities of the agents and skills selected through this expansion.
claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ agents skills rollout identity actions block menu; ExpandedContextIQ. Read Work IQ overview and Build skills for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. These document general capabilities, not the agents or skills exposed by this roadmap item.

claims.claim: No dedicated tenant UI switch or API for the expanded Context IQ menu choices is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ agents skills admin settings Graph default; Context IQ tenant disable PowerShell Graph menu. Read Agent settings, agent actions, registry, Business Applications default settings and Context IQ support; found general controls but no dedicated menu switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ agents skills content sources tenant switch default licensing Copilot Chat; Context IQ default agents. Read the roadmap, support article, Work IQ overview and agent settings; none states how this specific expansion is enabled or rolled out.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No licence requirement specific to enabling the new Context IQ menu interaction is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ expanded licensing price Copilot Credits agents; ExpandedContextIQ. Read Work IQ overview and Purchase and manage agents in Copilot Chat. General agent licences are documented, but no separate licence for this menu expansion is identified.

claims.claim: No separate price or meter for the new menu interaction is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ expanded licensing price Copilot Credits agents. Read Work IQ overview, Plan licensing and cost excerpts and Purchase and manage agents in Copilot Chat; these document API or agent usage, not a separate charge for the menu interaction.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview makes Work IQ available across Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents for licensed users, subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents. It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Work IQ API overview does not state that selecting an item in the Context IQ menu itself consumes credits.
claims.quote: Searched: Context IQ expanded licensing price Copilot Credits agents. Read the complete cited Work IQ overview; its pricing section describes Work IQ API usage and contains no Context IQ selection charge.

claims.claim: The cost of picking a custom or third-party agent in a prompt should be treated as wholly unconfirmed.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 (Basic) licenses, agents that access shared tenant data, such as SharePoint or Graph Connector content, are billed based on metered consumption.
claims.fix: Replace 'Treat the cost of picking a custom or third-party agent in a prompt as unconfirmed' with 'A separate charge for the new menu interaction is not published. Existing agent usage remains subject to published licensing and billing rules: agents accessing shared tenant data are metered for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 (Basic) licences, while declarative agents grounded in instructions and public websites are included.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/manage-agents-copilot-chat. Narrow the corresponding Open question to 'Does the new Context IQ menu interaction itself incur any additional charge?'

claims.claim: An administrator can select Agents > All agents > agent > Block in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **All agents**. ... In the **All agents** page, select an agent from the list of agents. ... In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.

claims.claim: The listed GET /v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages call is available for agent inventory without any stated licence prerequisite.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a [Microsoft Agent 365](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365) license.
claims.fix: Retain the GET endpoint, but add to controls[1].note and the corresponding prose: 'The Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence and CopilotPackages.Read.All permission (or CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackages-list in sources. The endpoint and GET method are documented; the missing licence qualification is the finding.

claims.claim: The registry documentation says the API works with the AI Admin Role.
claims.quote: The API works with the **AI Admin Role**.

claims.claim: The cited registry page presents the Graph inventory API as preview and shows the v1.0 packages endpoint with GET.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph API for Agent Registry and Agent Details (preview) ... $uri = "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages" ... $response = Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri $uri

claims.claim: The cited registry overview does not show a block API call.
claims.quote: Searched: the fetched agent-registry-overview text for Block and catalog/packages. Its Graph section documents GET packages and GET package details; the Block matches describe UI actions, not a block call.
